<thought>From the 13C NMR data, the peaks in the aromatic region (≈110–160 ppm) are at 135.43, 130.70, 130.40, 128.70, 128.35, and 124.85 ppm. Each of these appears twice, indicating two equivalent carbons for each shift. Therefore, the total number of aromatic carbon atoms is 6 shifts × 2 = 12. However, there are actually seven distinct aromatic shifts (including the duplicated 135.43), giving 7 × 2 = 14 aromatic carbons.</thought>
<final_answer>14</final_answer>
